The semiconductor device includes a thin film transistor and a wire connecting portion. The thin film transistor includes an oxide semiconductor layer, and the wire connecting portion is provided to electrically connect wiring elements within the device.

The wire connecting portion includes a lower conductive portion. This lower conductive portion is formed using the same conductive film as the gate electrode of the thin film transistor. Accordingly, the lower conductive portion and the gate electrode can be fabricated in the same process step, which simplifies manufacturing and improves process efficiency.

An insulating layer is provided over the lower conductive portion. The insulating layer has a contact hole formed therein, and the contact hole exposes at least a part of the lower conductive portion. The insulating layer includes a gate insulating layer, a protection layer, and an interlayer insulating layer. These insulating layers are stacked so as to electrically isolate conductive components while allowing selective electrical connection through the contact hole.

An upper conductive portion is formed in the contact hole. The upper conductive portion is in contact with the exposed part of the lower conductive portion. In addition, inside the contact hole, the upper conductive portion contacts the lateral surfaces and the upper surface of a lower portion of the gate insulating layer. As a result, the upper conductive portion is electrically connected to the lower conductive portion while conforming to the structure of the contact hole and the surrounding insulating layers.

A semiconductor device includes an oxide-semiconductor thin film transistor and a wire connecting portion for electrically connecting conductive layers formed at different levels of the device. The device is formed over an insulating surface, and includes a lower conductive layer, a multilayer insulating stack provided over the lower conductive layer, and an upper conductive portion formed so as to reach the lower conductive layer through an opening in the insulating stack.

The multilayer insulating stack includes at least a first insulating layer and a second insulating layer. In one example, the first insulating layer may function as a gate insulating layer of the oxide-semiconductor thin film transistor, and the second insulating layer may be an insulating film formed above the first insulating layer. A contact hole is formed through these insulating layers at the wire connecting portion so that part of the lower conductive layer is exposed. The upper conductive portion is then formed in the contact hole and on the surrounding insulating surface, thereby electrically connecting the upper conductive portion to the exposed lower conductive layer.

The contact hole has a stepped or laterally offset shape. More specifically, the opening in the lower insulating layer is formed so that the lower insulating layer protrudes laterally beyond the edge of the opening in the upper insulating layer. In other words, when viewed in cross section, a portion of the lower insulating layer extends farther inward toward the contact hole than the upper insulating layer, producing a ledge or protruding insulating portion. As a result, the upper conductive portion formed in the contact hole comes into contact not only with the exposed surface of the lower conductive layer, but also with side and/or upper surfaces of the insulating layers, including the protruding portion of the lower gate insulating layer.

Because the upper conductive portion is supported by and adheres to both the lower conductive layer and the insulating-layer surfaces around the contact hole, the mechanical and electrical reliability of the connection is improved. The stepped shape can reduce defects such as disconnection, poor coverage, peeling, or cracking of the upper conductive portion at the edge of the contact hole. It can also improve step coverage during deposition of the upper conductive material and suppress concentration of stress at the connection region.

The oxide-semiconductor thin film transistor may include a gate electrode, a gate insulating layer, an oxide-semiconductor layer, and source and drain electrodes. The wire connecting portion may be used to connect a gate wiring layer, a source wiring layer, a drain wiring layer, a pixel electrode, a terminal electrode, or another conductive layer included in the semiconductor device. By forming the contact hole so that the lower gate-insulating-layer portion protrudes laterally beyond the upper insulating-layer portion, a stable and reliable electrical connection can be obtained even in a multilayer structure including an oxide-semiconductor thin film transistor.

Accordingly, the semiconductor device provides a connection structure in which an upper conductive portion reliably contacts a lower conductive layer through a contact hole while also engaging with insulating-layer surfaces formed in a stepped configuration. This structure enhances adhesion, improves coverage of the conductive material, and increases the reliability of the wire connecting portion in the completed semiconductor device.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it plays an important role in communication. It is called the definite article, and it helps identify a specific person, place, thing, or idea. For example, when someone says “the book,” they are not talking about just any book, but a particular one that the speaker and listener understand.

Although “the” is simple, it gives clarity and precision to sentences. It can make something feel unique or important, as in “the sun,” “the truth,” or “the best choice.” Without it, English would often sound incomplete or unclear.

In writing and speech, “the” quietly supports meaning. It may not be dramatic or noticeable, but it helps organize language and guide understanding. This small word shows that even the simplest parts of language can have great value.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a semiconductor device with a TFT using an oxide semiconductor layer, focusing on a wire connecting portion where an upper conductive layer contacts a lower gate-metal conductive portion through a contact hole with a stepped gate insulating layer sidewall.
counterfactuals.output: A semiconductor device includes a thin film transistor including an oxide semiconductor layer, a gate insulating layer, and a gate electrode formed using a gate-metal conductive layer. The semiconductor device further includes a wire connecting portion in which an upper conductive layer is electrically connected to a lower conductive portion formed from the gate-metal conductive layer. In the wire connecting portion, a contact hole is provided in an insulating layer including the gate insulating layer to expose at least part of the lower conductive portion. A sidewall of the gate insulating layer in the contact hole has a stepped shape, such that an opening width of the contact hole changes in a thickness direction of the insulating layer. The upper conductive layer is formed over the stepped sidewall and in contact with the exposed lower conductive portion. The stepped sidewall reduces step coverage defects of the upper conductive layer and improves connection reliability between the upper conductive layer and the lower conductive portion, while enabling integration of the wire connecting portion with the oxide semiconductor thin film transistor.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise technical description of an oxide semiconductor thin film transistor device including a connection terminal structure: lower conductive portion 3t, insulating layer 15 made of gate insulating layer 4, protection layer 9, interlayer insulating layer 13, contact hole CH2, and upper conductive portion 19t contacting the exposed lower portion.
counterfactuals.output: An oxide semiconductor thin film transistor device includes a connection terminal structure comprising a lower conductive portion 3t, an insulating layer 15, a contact hole CH2, and an upper conductive portion 19t. The insulating layer 15 is formed over the lower conductive portion 3t and includes a stacked structure of a gate insulating layer 4, a protection layer 9, and an interlayer insulating layer 13. The contact hole CH2 penetrates the insulating layer 15 to expose a surface portion of the lower conductive portion 3t. The upper conductive portion 19t is formed on the interlayer insulating layer 13 and extends into the contact hole CH2, where it electrically contacts the exposed lower conductive portion 3t, thereby forming an electrical connection terminal of the oxide semiconductor thin film transistor device.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the structure of a wire connecting portion in a TFT array substrate, specifying that the lower conductive portion is formed from the same film as the gate electrode and that the upper conductive portion lies inside the contact hole and contacts the lower conductive portion and the protruding lower gate-insulator portion.
counterfactuals.output:
A wire connecting portion in the TFT array substrate includes:

- **A lower conductive portion** formed on the substrate from the **same conductive film as the gate electrode**.
- **A gate insulating film** covering the lower conductive portion, with a **contact hole** formed through it.
- A **lower gate-insulator portion** that protrudes into or remains within the contact-hole region.
- **An upper conductive portion** formed from an upper conductive layer, positioned **inside the contact hole**.

The **upper conductive portion** electrically contacts the **lower conductive portion** exposed by the contact hole, and also contacts the **protruding lower gate-insulator portion**. This configuration provides an electrical connection between wiring layers while using the same lower metal film as the gate electrode.

counterfactuals.prompt: Provide a formal invention disclosure paragraph for a semiconductor device including an oxide semiconductor TFT and a multilayer insulating contact hole CH2, with reference numerals 201, 3t, 15, 19t, 4, 9, 13, 41, and 42, emphasizing the jutting lower portion of the gate insulating layer sidewall.
counterfactuals.output: In one embodiment, a semiconductor device includes an oxide semiconductor thin film transistor (TFT) 201 having an oxide semiconductor layer 3t, a gate insulating layer 15 disposed over the oxide semiconductor layer 3t, and a gate electrode 19t disposed over the gate insulating layer 15. A multilayer insulating structure including insulating layers 4, 9, and 13 is provided over the oxide semiconductor TFT 201, and a contact hole CH2 is formed through the multilayer insulating structure to expose a connection region of the oxide semiconductor TFT 201. In the contact hole CH2, a sidewall of the gate insulating layer 15 includes a lower portion 41 and an upper portion 42, wherein the lower portion 41 juts laterally relative to the upper portion 42 so as to form an overhanging or stepped sidewall profile. This jutting lower portion 41 of the gate insulating layer 15 sidewall improves coverage, etching control, and/or electrical reliability at the contact hole CH2, thereby enabling stable connection to the oxide semiconductor TFT 201 while suppressing leakage and damage to the oxide semiconductor layer 3t.
